prerequisites: Shared seeded lab work2 (openlaw-docs-80ceef9e-work2) built from 067c1646829df85e62b809ee9157921e867c84e7; Helix seed light profile, random seed 7.

Provider mode: V-C21 only: a local OpenAI-compatible stand-in (contracts-b/provider-standin.mjs, a copy of DOC-029 analysis-standin/provider-standin.mjs that also parses the prompt's appended Response JSON Schema block) in its own container (node from the work2 app image) on the work2 backend network, alias doc030-cb-provider, no published port. Fictional paper with known extracted text and known answers. No real provider key or traffic. It is not a live-provider check.

Nadia Haddad (Legal Team Member) signs in with a password in an isolated Playwright Chromium context; Daniel Okafor is the concurrent editor; Ravi Menon (Business User) signs in to the Portal with a fresh magic link and submits the Requests.

Administrator API setup: AI connector pointed at the stand-in and enabled only for the walk, then removed; a DOC-030 Contract type whose Form gains three prompted record Field Rows; one live Counterparty. Acting-role API setup: Contracts C-279, C-280, C-281, C-282, C-285, C-297, C-323, C-324, PDF uploads and Versions, Request conversion, Ended status and restore, and one Document archive for the unavailable-citation check.
scenarios.expected: Evidence is tied to the chosen Document Version; confirming one value does not clear unrelated markers. Disabled connector, failed extraction, changed source, and stale evidence have the documented states. C43 separately verifies real provider setup.

limitations: Independent agent walkthrough by a different agent from the author and the technical source reviewer; not a human user study and not feature-owner approval.

V-C21 used a declared local OpenAI-compatible stand-in (contracts-b/provider-standin.mjs, adapted from DOC-029 analysis-standin) with fictional paper and known answers. It checks OpenLaw's workflow handling, not real provider setup, consent or model quality, and it does not satisfy C43. No external provider traffic occurred.

The shared work2 lab (openlaw-docs-80ceef9e-work2) had no AI connector. The connector pointed at the stand-in only during the two runs and was removed with its Saved key afterwards; the stand-in container was removed too.

The full run walked the guide at afdd6d9130ba438a92d2b14e4a13f587d1988fffdb2a129281a6dad959ce5741. The author then changed only the Analysis after Request conversion paragraph on Risk, Region and Department markers (guide 450aba9d948cd3c501b93a07ad336f621608c10a1e58668a6423b34fa0fb8fe3). That section was re-walked for both roles (run rewalk-450aba9d); the other steps keep their full-run times.

Request-context Analysis used Requests with no attachment; the runs read the Request title, description and urgency. A promoted Document Version, partial-source warnings, conflicts, restricted-source exclusion and switching the setting off were not exercised. Only Risk was filled among Risk, Region and Department; the guide's statement for Region and Department rests on the same code path.
The hidden Risk marker was read from the database (contracts.ai_unverified) as a state read, because the record API filters it out. This is recorded as a product bug in walkthrough.json.
Answer style's effect on a written value was not exercised; the stand-in returns fixed answers.
A retryable provider outage (HTTP 429 or 5xx) was not exercised; the terminal malformed-reply failure was.
The Ended stage, archive-to-restore, Document archive, team changes and Contract, upload and conversion setup used the API; every action the guide instructs was done in the browser.
Browser: Playwright 1.63.0 Chromium, headless, one context per identity at 1280x1600 CSS px; default theme only; no narrow layout, keyboard-only or assistive technology check.
